name: Cabeus
short: Water measured in the LCROSS impact plume at one spot.

evidence.finding: LCROSS measured water in debris blasted from one impact site in Cabeus; this does not confirm ice across the crater.
evidence.citation: Colaprete, A., et al. (2010). Detection of water in the LCROSS ejecta plume. Science 330, 463-468. doi:10.1126/science.1186986.

evidence.finding: M3 reported signs of surface ice in small permanently shaded patches inside this crater.
evidence.citation: Li, S., Lucey, P.G., Milliken, R.E., Hayne, P.O., Fisher, E., Williams, J.-P., Hurley, D.M., Elphic, R.C. (2018). Direct evidence of surface exposed water ice in the lunar polar regions. PNAS 115, 8907-8912. doi:10.1073/pnas.1802345115. Lemelin, M., Li, S., Mazarico, E., Siegler, M.A., Kring, D.A., Paige, D.A. (2021). Framework for Coordinated Efforts in the Exploration of Volatiles in the South Polar Region of the Moon. The Planetary Science Journal 2, 103. doi:10.3847/PSJ/abf3c5. Data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.4646092.

name: Amundsen
short: Cold traps are predicted here; no detection is mapped here.

evidence.instrument: LRO Diviner thermal model and LOLA shadow model
evidence.finding: Temperature and shadow maps predict cold traps here, but the reviewed map of reported ice signals has no detection assigned to this crater.
evidence.citation: Paige, D.A., et al. (2010). Diviner Lunar Radiometer observations of cold traps in the Moon's south polar region. Science 330, 479-482. doi:10.1126/science.1187726. Dataset: Paige et al. (2018), LRO DLRE Level 5 PRP V2.0, NASA PDS, LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0. Barker, M.K., Mazarico, E., Neumann, G.A., Smith, D.E., Zuber, M.T., Head, J.W., Sun, X. (2023). A New View of the Lunar South Pole from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA). The Planetary Science Journal 4, 183. doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1. Data doi:10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole.
